finding.title: Interrupted JSONL record newline can poison the next append and block output refresh
finding.mechanism: storage.append_observations writes each json.dumps(record) and '\n' in separate handle.write calls. A write error between them may leave a syntactically valid but unterminated JSON object at EOF; load_observations accepts it. A later append of a different observation writes directly after the old object, creating concatenated JSON objects on one line; subsequent load_observations raises ValueError. runner.run_once loads archive before publishing latest/audit/anata, so outputs can remain stale.
finding.deterministic_fixture: In tempfile seed G0 output files; create two distinct valid FlowObservation rows X,Y with finite values and legal timestamps. Inject OSError on the first newline write only, after complete JSON body X has been written and close has flushed it. Verify archive ends in '}' not '\n'. Retry append with Y and restore normal writes; also test retry [X,Y] and reverse X/Y. Use network=False and fixed as_of_ms.
expected_assertions: Recovery must never leave concatenated JSON objects on one line; every archived record must strict-json-parse separately.
A failed newline write must not result in a silently admitted or unrepairable half-committed record.
After corrected retry X and Y each appear exactly once, regardless of order, with provenance and original availability clocks intact.
latest.json, audit_latest.json and anata_latest.json must agree on one archive generation after recovery; no stale G0 outputs presented as current.
Unchanged exact-duplicate retry adds zero records; no change to point-in-time eligibility.
